# Collective Photon Fidelity

This repository studies single-temporal-mode Fock-state fidelity in ideal
Dicke emission and how excitation, loss, prefix detection, and coherent
control change its preparation resources. The scientific account is organized
by topic under science/.

## Authoritative files

- [README.md](README.md): question, principal results, science and learning
  routes, reproduction commands, purpose and contact.
- [science/model.md](science/model.md): source and field assumptions,
  normalized photon-number sectors, squared-fidelity convention, native
  theorem and connected scientific route.
- [science/native_emission.md](science/native_emission.md): exact wavefunction,
  constructive product-pulse bound, uniform median-count upper bound, and
  exact two-photon optimum.
- [science/partial_excitation.md](science/partial_excitation.md): the affine
  density family, explicit trial mode, relative-entropy minimizer, dilute and
  fixed-fraction limits, and near-inversion theorem including real a.
- [science/attenuation.md](science/attenuation.md): reduced survivor states,
  exact thinning identities, conditional fidelity ceiling and fixed-transmission
  target yield optimized over photon number and mode.
- [science/local_loss.md](science/local_loss.md): no-local-loss probability,
  exact normalized all-desired-photon kernel, fixed-loss scaling and
  exponential cost of strong native-source conditioning.
- [science/control_restrictions.md](science/control_restrictions.md): phase
  removal, reduced-state inequality, deterministic common clock, and ideal
  all-photon mode filtering.
- [science/prefix_detection.md](science/prefix_detection.md): recorded-origin
  prefix identity, consumed-photon law, detector stopping rule, nominal-target
  yield, trigger conditioning, and switching delay.
- [science/exact_fock_control.md](science/exact_fock_control.md): necessary and
  sufficient Markov-ladder criterion, phase compatibility, exact-emission
  time penalty and local-loss survival bound under the native rate cap.
- [science/capped_control.md](science/capped_control.md): coherent capped
  construction, finite-K fidelity and release-time bounds, local-loss acceptance
  and conditional fidelity, and accepted completion-time comparison.
- [science/numerical_checks.md](science/numerical_checks.md): amplitude
  recursion, normalization and cutoff conventions, numerical tables and
  independent comparisons.
- [science/interpretation.md](science/interpretation.md): why timing
  correlations constrain full-state fidelity and how the operations change
  the relevant state, record, photon number, time and yield.
- [references/RELATED_WORK.md](references/RELATED_WORK.md): primary-source
  roles and physical-model boundaries.
- [references/references.bib](references/references.bib): structured source
  metadata, including the single educational anchor.
- [verification/README.md](verification/README.md): environment, commands,
  benchmark coverage, reference output and limits of numerical evidence.
- [verification/check_fidelity.py](verification/check_fidelity.py):
  executable checks; --json reports residuals and analytical cutoff budgets.
- [verification/fidelity.py](verification/fidelity.py): normalized trial
  modes, ordered-amplitude recursion, loss probabilities and exact thinning.

## Reader routes

To understand the scientific story, start with model.md, follow native_emission.md
and partial_excitation.md, compare attenuation.md, local_loss.md and
prefix_detection.md, then read the three control pages and interpretation.md.

For an exact result, use the complete statement and proof on its topic page.
The explicit equation anchors are stable cross-reference targets. A README
summary, milestone target, trial pulse, or numerical example does not replace
the relevant proof or its assumptions.

For self-directed study, use the [30-milestone map](learning/MILESTONES.md)
alongside the [educational bridge](learning/BRIDGE.md). The common map has
14 background/preliminaries and 16 narrative/innovation milestones, with
project-defined targets, dependencies and conceptual connections.

The single selected anchor is Kiilerich and Mølmer, Quantum interactions with
pulses of radiation, Physical Review A 102, 023717 (2020), especially Sections
II A–C and III. The bridge translates the input–output and selected-mode
framework. The project's fidelity theorems are sourced to the science pages;
primary research citations retain their distinct attribution role.

To reproduce the calculations, read verification/README.md, install the root
requirements.txt dependencies, and run make check. Use the actual output;
the committed JSON is a reference run with ordinary floating-point values.

## Essential scientific distinctions

- Fock fidelity is a squared full-state overlap, not overlap amplitude,
  density-matrix purity or dominant-mode occupation.
- Keep sector probability, normalized conditional fidelity and unconditional
  target yield separate. A sector selection does not supply an operational
  herald without suitable monitoring or a success flag.
- M physical emitters with n symmetric excitations differ from a chosen subset
  of excited emitters. Real effective M in the local-loss kernel is a
  distributional parameter, not a fractional emitter count.
- The native theorem determines N^(-1/2) and bounding constants, not an exact
  prefactor. State dilute, fixed-fraction and near-inversion limits separately.
- Uniform optical attenuation gives reduced states of the ideal field.
  An actual local atomic jump can leave the symmetric spin sector.
- Prefix detection consumes photons, and the target mode uses the recorded
  time origin. The detector/latency formula concerns a specified nominal
  photon number and stopping rule.
- Common rate shaping preserves the ideal problem only through the stated
  complete clock transformation. Fixed physical local loss changes that case.
- Exact factorization under a rate cap and a sequence of fidelities approaching
  one are different requirements.
- The capped construction requires a single coherent output jump. Separate
  rate engineering or measured classical feedback does not alone implement it.
- Accepted completion time is conditional within a run; it is not a retry
  throughput or heralding-latency claim.
- Exact finite identities and floating-point benchmarks support the documented
  calculations. The analytical proofs establish uniform and asymptotic results.
